brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.evidence: 3 full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) with 3 bins; meshClash clear, house rules capOpenFaces + lockJoints applied
requirements.requirement: Compact tidy organizer for sewing supplies

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) + bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) for small notions; bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full open for larger tools
requirements.requirement: Separated compartments for small notions (buttons, bobbins, needles) plus space for larger tools

requirements.evidence: No thread spools, scissors, fabric or needle props in catalog (find_props for sewing/thread/scissor/fabric returned 0); staged with 2x solder-reel as thread/bobbin stand-ins, tweezers and tape measure visible from above

finish.summary: 3-cell desktop organizer: one 3-compartment bin, one 2-compartment bin, and one open bin for larger tools like a tape measure. Staged with thread-stand-in reels, tweezers and tape measure; no sewing-specific props exist in the catalog.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Sewing tidy coming up — I'll design a compact organizer for threads, tools, and notions.
